set.title: Industrial hazard procedures starter set
set.description: Four site emergency procedures written by Resgrid as a starting point for industrial and campus emergency response teams: chemical release and shelter in place, confined space rescue standby, lockout/tagout during an emergency, and hot work fire watch. Align them with your site's hazard assessments, permits and the occupational safety rules that apply to you.

protocols.name: Chemical release and shelter in place
protocols.description: Protecting people on site when a hazardous chemical is released, inside or outside the facility.

items.html: Move away from the release, upwind and uphill, and keep others away.
Raise the alarm and report the location, the product if known (label, placard, safety data sheet) and anyone hurt.
Only trained responders in the right protective equipment approach the release.

blocks.title: When told to shelter in place

items.html: Go indoors to the designated shelter rooms; close doors and windows.
Shut down ventilation that brings in outside air.
Account for everyone and report missing people to the incident commander.
Stay until the all-clear, then ventilate the building.

blocks.title: Know the product
blocks.html: Use the safety data sheet and your site's hazard information to choose protective equipment and decontamination.

protocols.name: Confined space rescue standby
protocols.description: The rescue team's duties while permit-required confined space entry is under way.

items.html: Review the entry permit, the space's hazards and the atmospheric readings.
Set up retrieval equipment and confirm the team can reach the space in the time the permit sets.
Agree communication signals with the attendant and the entrants.
Stay ready and in contact with the attendant; do not take other work.
On an alarm, start non-entry rescue with the retrieval system first.
Enter only with atmospheric monitoring and the protection the hazard requires.

blocks.title: Attendants do not enter
blocks.html: The attendant never enters the space to rescue; they call the rescue team.

protocols.name: Lockout/tagout during an emergency
protocols.description: Isolating energy when responders have to work on or near machinery during an emergency.

items.html: Find the machine's energy sources: electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical, thermal and chemical.
With site maintenance where possible, shut down and isolate each source and apply locks and tags.
Release or block stored energy (springs, raised parts, pressure).
Try to start the machine to confirm it is isolated, then return the controls to off.

blocks.title: Hand back
blocks.html: Record which locks responders applied and hand the isolation back to the site formally when the emergency ends.

protocols.name: Hot work fire watch
protocols.description: The fire watch's duties during and after welding, cutting and other hot work.

items.html: Check the hot work permit and that combustibles are moved away or covered.
Keep a suitable extinguisher at hand and know how to raise the alarm.
Watch for sparks and heat on both sides of walls, floors and ceilings.
Stay for the period your site sets after the work ends and check the area again before leaving.
